text:
Pius Suter does the quiet jobs for the Blues, and he's doing them well enough to chip in: 5 goals and 10 points in 23 games on 13:40 a night, with no power-play time to pad it. Undrafted out of Zurich, he's on his fourth NHL team and in his second season in St. Louis.

His finishing is running a little hot at 17.2%, above the top of our range for him, but the on-ice picture runs the other way: the Blues have scored about 4 fewer goals than expected with him out there. Taken together, his point total looks about right for what he does.

What he does, per Evolving-Hockey last season, is kill penalties (most of his value came on the PK) and push play forward: his team created more chances with him on, 87th percentile among forwards once linemates and zone starts are accounted for. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him on the end of 2.1 shots per 60 off passes across the slot or from behind the net, which is how a slow skater (9th percentile in top speed) scores. Our projection: 28 to 44 points.
